sa18:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa18:2.1: There was then a certain monk who rose from his seat.
sa18:2.2: He adjusted his robes to bare his right shoulder, bowed to the Buddha, and withdrew to stand at one side.
sa18:2.3: He then said to the Buddha,
sa18:2.4: “It would be good, Bhagavān, if you were to give me a brief explanation of the Dharma.
sa18:2.5: Having listened to the Dharma, I will go alone to a quiet place, focus on contemplation, and live earnestly … up to …
sa18:2.6: ‘He himself knows that he won’t be subject to a later existence.’”
sa18:3.1: The Bhagavān then told that monk,
sa18:3.3: ‘Bhagavān, give me a brief explanation of the Dharma.
sa18:3.4: Having listened to the Dharma, I’ll go alone to a quiet place, focus on contemplation, and live earnestly … up to …
sa18:3.5: “He himself knows that he won’t be subject to a later existence.”’ [Is this what you said?]”
sa18:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa18:5.2: “Listen closely! Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa18:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa18:5.4: If something doesn’t belong to you and it doesn’t belong to someone else, then this is something to get rid of quickly.
sa18:5.5: Once you’ve gotten rid of that thing, you will be benefited by this doctrine, and you’ll find happiness for a long time.”
sa18:6.1: That monk then said to the Buddha,
sa18:7.1: The Buddha said to the monk,
sa18:7.2: “How do you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full?”
sa18:8.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa18:8.2: “Bhagavān, form is not self, doesn’t belong to me, and doesn’t belong to someone else, so I should get rid of this thing quickly.
sa18:8.3: Having gotten rid of it, I will benefit by this doctrine, and I’ll find happiness for a long time.
sa18:8.4: Thus, feeling … conception … volition … awareness is not self, doesn’t belong to me, and doesn’t belong to someone else, so I should get rid of this thing quickly.
sa18:8.5: Having gotten rid of it, I will benefit by this doctrine, and I’ll find happiness for a long time.
sa18:8.6: Therefore, I understand the meaning of the Bhagavān’s brief explanation of the Dharma in full.”
sa18:9.2: “Good! It’s good, monk, that you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full.
sa18:9.4: Monk, form is not self, doesn’t belong to us, and doesn’t belong to someone else, so one should get rid of this thing quickly.
sa18:9.5: Having gotten rid of it, one will benefit by this doctrine, and they’ll find happiness for a long time.
sa18:9.6: Thus, feeling … conception … volition … awareness is not self, doesn’t belong to us, and doesn’t belong to someone else, so one should get rid of this thing quickly.
sa18:9.7: Having gotten rid of it, one will benefit by this doctrine, and they’ll find happiness for a long time.”
sa18:10.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he felt great joy.
sa18:10.2: He then bowed to the Buddha and withdrew.
sa18:10.3: He went alone to a quiet place where he diligently trained and lived earnestly … up to …
sa18:10.4: He himself knew that he wouldn’t be subject to a later existence.
sa18:11.1: That monk’s mind was liberated, and he became an arhat.
